newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's Ryanair to join Irish/U.S. stock markets.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Ryanair to join Irish/U.S. stock markets.

text.p: Ireland's 'low-budget' airline Ryanair announced on Tuesday it wanted to float on the Irish stock exchange and the Nasdaq in the United States, the first Irish company to seek a simultaneous quote on both sides of the Atlantic.

Ryanair is offering approximately 54.2 million shares at between 165 Irish pence ($2.46) and 195 Irish pence for a market capitalisation of 261.2 million Irish pounds ($389.4 million) to 308.7 million Irish pounds.
"Our secret is low fares, low fares and even more low fares. No meals, no frills, no newspapers, no nuts," chief executive Michael O'Leary told reporters at the announcement of the flotation.
Ryanair, which has been operating for 12 years and has a fleet of 17 Boeing 737-200 aircraft, said the funds will be used to cut debt, which is now 35 million Irish pounds.
It will also allow the airline to be in a position to buy aircraft when necessary, it said.
Speculation the company would seek a listing mounted after U.S. entrepreneur David Bonderman became Ryanair chairman in December 1996 after taking a 20 percent stake in the airline.

Bonderman took over from former GPA chief Tony Ryan whose family founded Ryanair. After the offer, the Ryan family will own 35.3 percent of the company, down from 61.7 percent, while Irish Air and chief executive Michael O'Leary will own 15.7 and 14.1 percent, respectively. The flotation will comprise an offer of shares to investors in Ireland, a public offer in the U.S. and offers to professional investors in the UK and Continental Europe, Ryanair said.
Ryanair said its strategy was to aim for 20 to 30 percent sales growth a year and increase flights on existing routes.
Morgan Stanley & Co International Ltd have been appointed Global co-ordinator and bookrunner for the issue.

The offer will be underwritten by Morgan Stanley, Investment Bank of Ireland, CS First Boston and the Robinson Humphrey Company, Inc. Morgan Stanley and IBI Corporate Finance will act as joint sponsors and financial advisers to Ryanair and Davy Stockbrokers will be brokers to the issue.
